basis: Eating disorder; psychiatric conditions have no axis. Associated obesity and metabolic diseases are separate diagnoses.
Immunodeficiency with defining autoimmune cytopenias; vitiligo represents melanocyte loss in 1/1 reported patient. Recurrent infections are separate episodes.
Neoplasm arising in the external ear; no additional organ involvement applies across the umbrella.
Predominantly ovarian or testicular germ cell tumors, outside the axes; extragonadal subtypes have different sites and do not establish a common covered organ.
Hepatic heme-synthesis disorder defined by neurovisceral attacks; HPO reports skin scarring in 30-79%, although photosensitivity and blistering are less frequent.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and dilated cardiomyopathy define the disorder; hypotonia alone does not establish primary muscle damage.
Cortical dysplasia, epilepsy and developmental regression define disease; strabismus affects 3/3 assessed patients. Constipation alone does not establish intestinal damage.
Methionine metabolic disorder with encephalopathy and liver dysfunction; muscle atrophy 2/2 and elevated CK 3/6 support myopathy. Cardiac defects and hearing loss (~33%) omitted by cap.
Inherited myopia is an ocular refractive and growth disorder.
Acquired red cell aplasia causes impaired marrow erythropoiesis and anemia; an immune mechanism is not established by the supplied record.
Hantavirus infection defined by renal injury and hemorrhagic hematologic dysfunction, including thrombocytopenia; blurred vision alone does not establish ocular damage.
Lacrimal gland disease belongs to the ocular axis; immune mechanisms apply to particular subtypes rather than the whole umbrella.
Craniosynostosis and eyelid/ocular malformations characterize the syndrome. Frequencies of developmental impairment and cardiac defects are unspecified, so additional axes are withheld.
Congenital displacement of the pupil is an ocular malformation.
Defined by intellectual disability; developmental delay, seizures and cortical abnormalities support neurologic involvement. Genital anomalies have no axis.
Epithelial neoplasm arising in the urethra, which belongs to the renal axis; villous architecture does not imply gastrointestinal origin.
Defined by congenital joint contractures together with lissencephaly, establishing musculoskeletal and neurologic disease.
Inherited cervical arterial dissection is a vascular disorder; associated ischemic stroke is a separately diagnosed complication.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with leukodystrophy; contractures occur in 30-79% and arthrogryposis in 2/2. Optic atrophy is <30%; respiratory failure lacks evidence of direct lung injury.
Dopamine transporter dysfunction causes infantile parkinsonism-dystonia. Ocular flutter is a neurologic movement sign; feeding difficulty does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Neuropathy/dysmyelination, deafness and aganglionosis define disease; lacrimal dysfunction occurs in ~67%. Common skin pigment abnormalities and hypogonadism (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Lysosomal storage affects liver and spleen; interstitial lung disease is common, with reduced DLCO in 5/8. Bone loss (30-79%) omitted by cap; cherry-red spots alone do not impair vision.
Dental agenesis/microdontia with an inherited endocrine growth disorder; strabismus is a defining syndromic feature. Borderline intellect alone does not establish intellectual disability.
Motor neuron disease causes defining scapuloperoneal denervation and muscle atrophy in most patients. Respiratory muscle weakness alone does not establish direct lung damage.
ASXL3 neurodevelopmental disorder; strabismus occurs in 7/12 (~58%). Feeding difficulties and hypotonia do not establish separate gastrointestinal or muscle damage.
